task:
READ-ONLY code review - do NOT modify any files. Repo: /home/justinlime/code/wyomingchat (Python/PySide6 voice bridge using the Wyoming protocol over TCP).

BUG REPORT: TTS audio only plays after the final chunk is received, instead of playing each chunk as it arrives.

Read carefully:
- src/wyomingchat/clients.py TextToSpeechSession._read_loop and WyomingTcpConnection: how audio-start, audio-chunk, and audio-stop events are decoded and how the on_audio_start/on_audio_chunk/on_complete callbacks are invoked (which thread, how often).
- src/wyomingchat/wyoming_protocol.py: encode_event/decode_event and read_exactly - confirm the framing delivers each event independently (no accidental buffering of the whole payload).
- The controller lambdas passed as callbacks in _start_tts (controller.py) that emit PySide6 Signals from the reader thread.

Answer with file:line references: (1) Does the reader deliver audio-chunk callbacks immediately per event, or could the socket reads block/accumulate until audio-stop? (2) Is there any per-event payload buffering in decode_event/read_exactly? (3) Could PySide6 queued signal delivery between the reader thread and GUI thread reorder or delay chunks, and is the audio-start signal guaranteed before chunks? (4) Any way the reader thread gets starved (GIL, blocking sendall on the same socket in the writer thread) so that chunks accumulate server-side and arrive in one burst at the end? (5) Recommend the minimal fix to guarantee per-chunk streaming playback.

Return a concise findings report with file:line references.

criteriaSatisfied.evidence: Concrete findings with file:line references and severities returned in /tmp/review_playback2.txt and summarized below: (1) Reader delivers callbacks immediately per event — clients.py:634-677, _on_audio_chunk at 666-668, no deferral to audio-stop (670); verified with a real loopback TCP server (paced chunks arrived paced, blast chunks arrived as a burst mirroring the server). (2) No per-event buffering — wyoming_protocol.py:65-92 decode_event reads one header line (69) plus exact data_length/payload_length via read_exactly (95-111, loop at 101); each event independently framed; makefile internal buffering (clients.py:146) does not merge events. (3) Queued-signal order guaranteed FIFO (controller.py:613-614 lambdas emit from tts-reader thread; connects at 148-149; audio-start emitted clients.py:656-663 before chunks 666-668) — verified with PySide6; delay possible when the GUI loop is busy: all queued chunk slots then fire in a 0.0-gap burst when the loop unblocks (verified), which is the mechanism matching the reported symptom. (4) No reader starvation: single TTS reader thread, no writer thread (unlike STT clients.py:396), one uncontended sendall before the read loop (clients.py:643-647), GIL released during blocking reads; actual risk is the reader running AHEAD of the GUI with no backpressure. (5) Minimal fix recommended: buffer pre-start chunks instead of dropping (controller.py:695-705 + audio.py:475-478 silent-drop hazard, medium) and add a per-chunk acknowledgement for bounded backpressure; note server-side full-synthesis buffering cannot be fixed client-side. Severities: no defect in protocol framing/TTS read loop; medium for the silent chunk-drop and for the unbounded queued-signal burst.

residualRisks: If the Wyoming TTS server buffers the entire synthesis and emits all audio-chunk events only at the end, no client change can produce streaming playback; the client already mirrors server pacing exactly.

The pre-start silent chunk-drop path (controller.py:695-705 + audio.py:475-478) is normally masked by FIFO signal ordering but becomes data loss if ordering is ever violated (e.g., future multi-thread emission).
Playback writes remain on the GUI thread (QAudioSink created in _handle_tts_audio_start); the recommended backpressure fix paces the reader but does not move sink writes off the GUI event loop.
Empirical PySide6 checks ran headless with QCoreApplication (QtMultimedia/QAudioSink unavailable in this sandbox); actual sink write/blocking behavior on Linux/Windows was not exercised.

reviewFindings: info: clients.py:634-677 — TTS read loop decodes and dispatches each event immediately; no accumulation until audio-stop (verified empirically).
info: wyoming_protocol.py:65-111 — decode_event/read_exactly frame each event independently; no per-event payload buffering.

medium: controller.py:613-614 + clients.py:666-668 — no backpressure between tts-reader thread and GUI; queued chunk signals pile up and are delivered in an end-of-stream burst when the GUI loop is busy, matching the reported symptom (verified empirically).
medium: controller.py:695-705 + audio.py:475-478 — chunk handed to write_audio before start_stream is silently dropped (returns 0); latent data-loss hazard normally masked by FIFO ordering.
info: controller.py:613-614 + clients.py:656-663 — audio-start is emitted before chunks and PySide6 queued delivery preserves FIFO order, so audio-start is guaranteed delivered first.
info: clients.py:634-677 — single TTS reader thread, no writer thread, uncontended sendall; no GIL/socket starvation path; reader runs ahead of the GUI rather than being starved.

recommendation: buffer pre-start chunks and flush after start_stream; add a per-chunk acknowledgement (threading.Event) so the reader paces socket reads to GUI consumption, guaranteeing incremental playback and pushing accumulation back to the server via TCP backpressure.
